item: player-controls: (1) the favourite heart in the 3-button toggle row doesn't update until shuffle or repeat is touched; (2) the previous/next press morph takes longer than play/pause; (3) remove "Now Playing" and the cloud from the full player's top bar and show the connected output device's name there
currentBehaviour:
(1) Favourite. NowPlayingView.swift:100 computes `let isFavorite = library.song(id: song.id)?.isFavorite ?? song.isFavorite` inside `controls(_:)`, which runs inside NowPlayingView.body (body:33-39 → content:41 → controls:71/99). `LibraryStore.song(id:)` (App/Stores/LibraryStore.swift:50) returns `songsById[id]`, and `songsById` is `@ObservationIgnored` (LibraryStore.swift:25). So that read is not tracked, and NowPlayingView never subscribes to library changes.

Tapping the heart calls `env.libraryEditor.toggleFavorite(song.id)` (NowPlayingView.swift:114 → App/Features/Library/LibraryEditing.swift:110-126 → commit:258-260 → `LibraryStore.applyEdit`, LibraryStore.swift:111-120). applyEdit patches `songsById` in place (ignored) and bumps `snapshot` and `revision` (both tracked). NowPlayingView.body reads neither. It does read `playback.isShuffleEnabled` and `playback.repeatMode` (NowPlayingView.swift:110-113, tracked on @Observable PlaybackStore, App/Stores/PlaybackStore.swift:11,23-24), and also `playback.isPlaying`/`current`. So tapping shuffle or repeat (or play/pause, or a song change) re-runs the body, which reads the fresh `songsById` and only then shows the new heart. That matches Hoa's symptom.

PlayerToggleRow (App/Features/NowPlaying/PlayerToggleRow.swift:11-68) is a plain value view and is fine. History: `songsById` has been ignored since stage 4 (6a2c3f7). The full player's heart that reads it arrived in stage 8 (c6bc18f), so the bug dates from c6bc18f.

Other places:
- The lyrics More sheet has the same pattern. LyricsView.swift:368 (inside the `.sheet` content closure, :199/:359) and LyricsOptionsSheet's body (LyricsView.swift:636) pass `env.libraryEditor.isFavorite(...)` (LibraryEditing.swift:108 → `store.song(id:)`, the same ignored lookup). LyricsMoreSheet stores it as `let isFavorite` (LyricsMoreSheet.swift:35) and shows it at :176, inside `private var toggleRow` (:170).
- SongOptionsSheet uses the same pattern: body:32 `library.song(id: songId)`, options():114 `song.isFavorite`, toggle at :131. Nothing else in that body reads tracked library state. Same mechanism, not reported by Hoa.
- Not affected: MiniPlayerBar (App/DesignSystem/Components/MiniPlayerBar.swift has no heart); library rows and the Liked tab (LibraryModel compares inputs by `revision`, LibraryModel.swift:28-35,124); SongMultiSelectionSheet (LibrarySheets.swift:405), which dismisses on tap.
- The lock-screen like is never wired. `NowPlayingController.onLike`/`isFavorite` (App/Playback/NowPlayingController.swift:20-22) are never assigned (AppEnvironment.swift:171-179 sets only `remote`), so `likeCommand.isEnabled = false` (:175). parity.md:8 says "like waits for a favourites API".

(2) Morph timing. AnimatedPlaybackControls.swift uses one press spring for all three pills, `pressSpring` = interpolatingSpring(mass 1, stiffness 800, damping 2·0.6·√800 ≈ 33.9) (lines 39-41, applied at :80). That gives a ≈0.22 s period and damping ratio 0.6. The pressed pill goes to weight 1.1 and the others to 0.65 (:96-106). The settle-back is delayed in `.task(id: clickCount)`, line 68: `let delay: Duration = control == .playPause ? .milliseconds(220) : .milliseconds(600)`.

The delay timer starts at the tap, so it runs at the same time as the grow:
- play/pause: grow ≈0–0.23 s, release starts at 0.22 s, ≈0.45 s in total;
- skip: grow ≈0–0.23 s, held squeezed until 0.6 s, release done ≈0.83 s.
So a skip stays morphed about 380 ms longer. The doc comment at :4-5 says so.

This is a faithful port of Android's hold: AnimatedPlaybackControls.kt:96-105 (`NEXT, PREVIOUS -> 600L else -> releaseDelay`), releaseDelay 220L (FullPlayerContent.kt:1217), and `pressAnimationSpec = motionScheme.fastSpatialSpec()` (FullPlayerContent.kt:1182). The newest Android branch, origin/android-int-oct3, has the same values (kt:103, FullPlayerContent.kt:1316/1375). The 180 ms deferral of onNext/onPrevious exists only on the older main-6hltyd Android lineage (kt:160-163, 242-245). android-int-oct3 calls them immediately (kt:173-176), as iOS does (:82).

Play/pause's corner morph is a separate `.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.8)` on `isPlaying` (:64). Skips don't flip isPlaying (DualDeckEngine.jump:435-446 keeps playWhenReady), so that spring is not involved.

(3) Top bar. NowPlayingView.swift:147-267 `PlayerTopBar(song:)`, built at :45. It is a 64 pt HStack(spacing 0) of:
- a 56 pt nav slot with the 42 pt collapse circle, leading 4 (:166-181);
- "Now Playing" (`labelLarge` semibold), plus `cloud.fill` 14 pt when `isStreamed(song)` (:182-194, leading 18);
- `Spacer(minLength: 8)` (:195);
- an HStack(spacing 6) holding the output pill and the 50×42 queue pill, trailing 18 (:196-213).

The output pill (:218-261):
- Label: shows only for Spotify Connect (`env.spotifyConnect.active?.name`) or AirPlay (`route.isRemote && !route.name.isEmpty`; AudioRouteMonitor.swift:84; `isRemote` has no other caller).
- Width: frame `minWidth 50, maxWidth showsLabel ? 190 : 58` (:241). With both min and max, the frame takes the proposal clamped, so icon-only renders 58 pt, while Android's wrapped widthIn(50..58) gives 50.
- Corners: 21 on the leading side; on the trailing side 21 with a label and 6 without (:226,246-248).
- An 8 pt `onTertiaryContainer` dot whenever a label shows (:235).
- Connect context menu (:250-256), spring (0.5, 0.6) on showsLabel (:257).
- VoiceOver: "Playing on <name>" for Connect, otherwise "AirPlay", "Bluetooth" or "Local playback" (:258-259); id `player.devices`.
The `song` parameter is used only by `isStreamed` (:264-266).

AudioRouteMonitor (AudioRouteMonitor.swift:8-85) is @Observable with:
- `kind`: phone (builtInSpeaker, builtInReceiver or nil), headphones, bluetooth, airPlay, carAudio, other;
- `name` = `currentRoute.outputs.first?.portName`, refreshed on routeChangeNotification (:33-36,55-69).
DevicesSheet.swift:182-198 has private `outputTitle`/`outputSubtitle` ("This phone", "Local playback", "Headphones", "Bluetooth audio", "AirPlay", "Car audio", "Audio output"); outputSubtitle is used at :151.

UI tests that depend on the bar:
- SpotifyConnectScreenshotTests.testNowPlayingChipLight (UITests/SpotifyConnectScreenshotTests.swift:73-80) asserts an element labelled exactly "Playing on Kitchen Echo Show".
- GlassAccessibilityTests.testPlayerTopBarKeepsButtonTraits (:30-35) checks "Collapse player".
- No test or string-catalog entry references "Now Playing" or "Cloud stream" (App/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings has no such keys).

Android (FullPlayerContent.kt:711-890, main-6hltyd):
- The title and cloud are wrapped in `if (!isCastConnecting) AnimatedVisibility(visible = !isRemotePlaybackActive)` (:724-725; oct3 :783), so Android already hides "Now Playing" while casting to make room. The iOS port always shows it.
- The cast pill is labelled only while casting or connecting (showCastLabel, :781), with max width 190 and the dot only while remote (:878).
rootCause:
(1) Proven by the code. The favourite flag is read through `LibraryStore.songsById`, which is `@ObservationIgnored` (LibraryStore.swift:25; read at :50). `applyEdit` (LibraryStore.swift:111-120) mutates only that ignored dictionary plus `snapshot` and `revision`, and NowPlayingView.body (NowPlayingView.swift:100) never reads `snapshot` or `revision`. So Observation never invalidates the full player after a favourite edit. The next unrelated tracked change, such as shuffle or repeat (`playback.isShuffleEnabled`/`repeatMode` read at :110-113), re-runs the body, and the new value then appears. Apple: ObservationIgnored "Disables observation tracking of a property" (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/observation/observationignored()).

Ruled out:
- PlayerToggleRow has no Equatable or memo.
- The write is synchronous: `store.applyEdit` runs before the detached persistence task (LibraryEditing.swift:260-263).
- isPlaying does not change.
- Nothing applies `.id(...)` to the player.

(2) Not a bug but a ported constant: the 600 ms hold for previous/next at AnimatedPlaybackControls.swift:68, against 220 ms for play/pause. The timer overlaps the ≈0.23 s grow, so skips stay morphed for ≈0.83 s against ≈0.45 s.

options.name: Favourite fix A (recommended): observed lookup + small child view
options.description: Add `LibraryStore.observedSong(id:)`, which reads `revision` and then `songsById`. Move the toggle row's state reads into a private child view `PlayerToggles` in NowPlayingView.swift, so only that row re-renders on library edits and on shuffle/repeat changes. Point SongOptionsSheet and LyricsMoreSheet's own body at the observed lookup. Leave `LibraryEditor.isFavorite` unchanged.
options.pros: Smallest fix and consistent with the existing 'key on library.revision' rule (docs/performance.md:87). Also fixes the lyrics More sheet and the song sheet. The full player's body stops re-running on shuffle/repeat taps.
options.cons: The row re-renders on every library revision (artist-image batches, rescans). That is cheap because it is one small view. It touches a shared file (Stores/*: docs/design.md:225-227), so it needs a small commit with a stated reason.

options.name: Favourite fix B: observable favouriteIds set on LibraryStore
options.description: Keep a tracked `private(set) var favoriteIds: Set<String>`, rebuilt in install() and patched in applyEdit when changedSongs flip isFavorite. Hearts read `library.favoriteIds.contains(id)`.
options.pros: Hearts re-render only on favourite changes, not on unrelated revisions.
options.cons: More code in a shared store, and a second source of truth to keep in sync with the snapshot, backup restore (BackupService.swift:341) and Spotify/YouTube likes (SpotifyService.swift:416,431; YouTubeMusicSearchProvider.swift:66).

options.name: Favourite fix C: just read `library.revision` in NowPlayingView.body
options.pros: One line, and no shared-file edit.
options.cons: The whole pre-built full player (carousel, seek bar, ambient background) re-runs its body on every library revision, including Deezer artist-image batches during browsing. It goes against the idle-cost goals in docs/performance.md:159.

options.name: Top bar A (recommended): output pill grows into the freed space
options.description: Delete the title and cloud. Keep the pill right-aligned and joined to the queue pill (the Android split-button look). With a label it becomes a full capsule that hugs its text and may grow into the freed width: the right-hand cluster gets layoutPriority 1, and the label truncates at the tail. The label shows for any non-built-in output (Connect, AirPlay, Bluetooth, wired, car); on the phone's own speaker the pill is icon-only.
options.pros: Re-uses the existing morphing pill, keeps the Spotify Connect UI test label, and extends what Android already does while casting (it hides the title then, FullPlayerContent.kt:724-725).
options.cons: Diverges from Android, which labels only cast and shows the title otherwise. Hoa asked for this.

options.name: Top bar B: device name where the title was
options.description: Put an icon + name text (or a glass capsule) left-aligned after the collapse circle, and keep the right-side output pill icon-only.
options.pros: The name reads first, like a title.
options.cons: Two controls for one thing (a name chip and an output button), and more clutter. The Connect 'Playing on' label test and the context menu would have to move.

recommendedPlan.change: Do NOT change `isFavorite` (line 108). It is used by `toggleFavorite` (an action, outside any body) and as the fallback argument to LyricsMoreSheet. LyricsMoreSheet will read the live value in its own body (below). If it were made observed, the `.sheet` content closure in LyricsView (:199 → moreSheet :359-368) would add a `revision` dependency wherever SwiftUI attributes that closure's reads, possibly the heavy karaoke LyricsView, for no gain.

Line 32 (body): change `if let song = library.song(id: songId)` to `if let song = library.observedSong(id: songId)`. The heart at :114-133 then flips immediately, and its `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: isFavorite)` plays. The sheet is a single view, so the extra revision dependency is cheap.

Make the heart independent of how the presenter's sheet closure is tracked:
- Add `@Environment(LibraryStore.self) private var library`. It is injected at the app root (App/PixlAudioApp.swift:14), so it is present in sheets and covers.
- `toggleRow` (:170) is a plain computed property, not a @ViewBuilder. So add `let liked = song.flatMap { library.observedSong(id: $0.id)?.isFavorite } ?? isFavorite` as its first line, and change the existing `HStack(spacing: 8) {` to `return HStack(spacing: 8) {`, or it won't compile.
- Use `liked` in place of `isFavorite` in the favourite `toggle(...)` at :176 (active, systemImage).
- Keep the `isFavorite` init parameter (:35) as the fallback, so both callers (LyricsView.swift:360, :630) stay untouched.
Coordinate with the lyrics-page work item: it edits this file too (the 'Keep screen on' switch at :165, the static/synced controls).

Line 68: replace the per-control delay with one constant, matching play/pause.
- Add `private static let releaseDelay: Duration = .milliseconds(220)` next to `pressSpring` (:39-41).
- In the task (:66-72): `guard lastClicked != nil else { return }`, then `try? await Task.sleep(for: Self.releaseDelay)`. The `control` binding is no longer needed. `Self.pressSpring` is already read in the same task, so the isolation is identical.
- Keep `pressSpring` exactly as it is (stiffness 800, damping ≈ 33.94: ≈0.22 s period, damping ratio 0.6) for both the grow and the release.

Result: the timer starts at the tap and overlaps the grow, so every pill takes about 0.45 s from tap to settled, against about 0.83 s for skips today. Reduce Motion is unchanged: `lastClicked` stays nil, and the task returns early.

Update the doc comment at :4-5 to: '…then they settle back 220 ms after any press (Hoa, 2026-10-07: skips match play/pause; Android holds a skip 600 ms) on Android's fast spatial spring.'

Top bar (owner override of parity).

(a) Line 45: `PlayerTopBar()`. Remove `let song: Song` (:149) and `static func isStreamed` (:263-266); only :187 used them. The top bar then no longer re-renders on song changes.

(b) Delete the title HStack at :182-194 ('Now Playing' and the cloud) and change :195 to `Spacer(minLength: 12)`.

(c) REQUIRED, and this corrects the previous plan: put `.layoutPriority(1)` on the right-hand cluster, i.e. after `.padding(.trailing, 18)` at :213. layoutPriority acts only among the siblings of the immediate parent stack: 'Views typically have a default priority of 0 which causes space to be apportioned evenly to all sibling views … A parent layout offers the child views with the highest layout priority all the space offered to the parent minus the minimum space required for all its lower-priority children' (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/layoutpriority(_:)). Priority on the pill alone would only rank it against the queue button inside the inner HStack. The cluster would still split the leftover width with the Spacer, so a Connect name would truncate around 90 pt on a 393 pt phone. With the cluster at priority 1, the pill can use width − 60 (nav) − 12 (Spacer) − 18 (trailing) − 6 (gap) − 50 (queue) = width − 146: about 229 pt on 375, 247 on 393, 256 on 402, 294 on 440. Adding `.layoutPriority(1)` on the pill too is harmless; the queue button is fixed at 50.

(d) Rewrite `outputPill` (:220-261):
- `let connect = env.spotifyConnect.active`
- `let label: String? = connect?.name ?? route.deviceName`
- `let isRemote = connect != nil || route.isRemote`
- `let showsLabel = label != nil`; trailing radius `showsLabel ? 21 : 6` (unchanged).
- Label HStack(spacing 8): icon 18 pt semibold (`connect?.symbolName ?? route.systemImage`); then `Text(label).pixlFont(.labelMedium).lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.tail)` (verbatim String, as today); then the 8 pt `onTertiaryContainer` dot only `if isRemote` (Android: dot only while remote, kt:878).
- Padding: leading 14, trailing `showsLabel ? 16 : 14` (unchanged).
- Frame: replace `.frame(minWidth: 50, maxWidth: showsLabel ? 190 : 58, minHeight: 42, maxHeight: 42, alignment: .leading)` with `.frame(minWidth: 50, minHeight: 42, maxHeight: 42, alignment: .leading)`. With only a minimum, the frame hugs its content (at least 50), so icon-only becomes 50 pt like Android's wrapped 50 dp and the queue pill (today 58). The 190 pt cap goes.
- Animate on the value, not just its presence: `.animation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.6), value: label)`, so switching from AirPods to a speaker re-sizes smoothly. Optionally add `.contentTransition(.opacity)` on the Text (already used in App, e.g. LibrarySheets.swift:168).
- Accessibility: `.accessibilityLabel(label.map { String(localized: "Playing on \($0)") } ?? String(localized: "Playing on this phone"))`, which keeps 'Playing on Kitchen Echo Show' for SpotifyConnectScreenshotTests:76. Add `.accessibilityHint("Opens the devices sheet")`. Keep id `player.devices` and the Connect context menu (:250-256) unchanged.
- Optional (Android parity for `isCastConnecting`, kt:848/870): while `connect == nil && env.spotifyConnect.connectingDeviceId != nil` (SpotifyConnectController.swift:45, observable), show `String(localized: "Connecting…")` plus a ProgressView with `.controlSize(.mini)` in place of the name.

(e) Update the doc comments at :6-7 ('top bar (64 pt): the collapse circle (42 pt) and on the right the output pill — the output's icon, plus the device's name for any output other than this phone (Spotify Connect, AirPlay, Bluetooth, wired, car) — and the queue pill') and at :218-223 (drop the 'shares the top bar with "Now Playing"' note).

2. Find `app.descendants(matching: .any).matching(identifier: "player.favorite").firstMatch`. Use descendants, not `app.buttons`, in case the glass changes the element type. Wait until it exists and `isHittable`: the pre-built player also carries `screen.nowPlaying` while collapsed.

design.md:
- Player section (~:343) and the Spotify Connect 'Chip' bullet (:727): the top bar has no title or cloud; the output pill names any non-phone output and may use the freed width; skips settle 220 ms like play/pause; these are owner overrides of parity (2026-10-07).

parity.md:
- Row 43 (player sheet): note the same divergences.
- Keep row 8's 'like waits for a favourites API' unless the lock-screen like gets wired.

Add a dated handoff note in docs/handoff/ that names the shared-file edits (LibraryStore, UITestLaunchRouter).

No new Apple APIs: layoutPriority (SongOptionsSheet.swift:155), truncationMode (GenreBrowseView.swift:225), contentTransition(.opacity) (LibrarySheets.swift:168) and accessibilityHint are already used in App/, and portName/currentRoute/Port are ledgered (api-notes.md:246,434).

risks: `observedSong` adds a dependency on `revision`. Revision also bumps on artist-image batches (`updateArtists`, LibraryStore.swift:124-135), rescans and every edit, so PlayerToggles, SongOptionsSheet and LyricsMoreSheet re-render then. That is cheap for these small views, but never call it from list rows, NowPlayingView.body itself or LyricsView.

Nobody can compile locally. `_ = revision` inside an @Observable class method goes through the macro-generated getter, which registers access; it is valid Swift and gives no warning. The LyricsMoreSheet `toggleRow` edit needs an explicit `return`: it is not a @ViewBuilder. Verify both on CI.

Top-bar layout is unverified without a simulator. If `.layoutPriority(1)` ends up only on the pill and not on the right-hand cluster, long names truncate at roughly half the free width. Check the SpotifyConnect chip screenshots at 375 pt and 440 pt.

A song that isn't in the library snapshot (e.g. a streamed song not yet imported) falls back to `song.isFavorite` from the queue entry. `setFavorite` only edits songs in the snapshot (LibraryEditing.swift:119-121), so the heart can't flip for such songs. That is pre-existing, and the fix doesn't change it.

Without a cap, very long Bluetooth or AirPlay names (e.g. 'Hoa’s AirPods Pro – Find My') fill most of the bar and truncate with an ellipsis, 12 pt from the collapse circle. Acceptable, but look at it on the 375 pt width.
The icon-only output pill shrinks from 58 to 50 pt, a visible change in the expanded-player screenshots. It matches Android's wrapped 50 dp.
Shared files (docs/design.md:225-227): LibraryStore.swift and UITestLaunchRouter.swift need small separate commits with a stated reason, mentioned in the handoff note.
LyricsMoreSheet is also touched by the lyrics-page item (static/synced buttons, keep-screen-on toggle at :165). Merge carefully.
Removing `song` from PlayerTopBar: only `isStreamed` used it (NowPlayingView.swift:187). The 'Cloud stream' label goes with it; no test references it.

The 220 ms hold starts at the tap, while the ≈0.23 s grow is still finishing. If Hoa wants it even quicker (e.g. 150 ms), the squeeze will be interrupted before it peaks. That is fine with an interruptible spring, but it reads as a smaller bounce.
ownerDecisions: On the phone's own speaker, what should the output pill show? (a) Icon only (recommended, least clutter, same as today); (b) icon + 'This phone'; (c) icon + 'iPhone'.

Should wired headphones, Bluetooth and car outputs show their name in the top bar (recommended: yes, e.g. 'AirPods Pro'), or only outputs that play elsewhere (AirPlay or Spotify Connect, like Android)?
Keep the device name inside the right-hand output pill next to the queue button (recommended), or move it to the left where 'Now Playing' was?
Previous and next: settle back 220 ms after the tap exactly like play/pause (recommended, ≈0.45 s in total), or even quicker (e.g. 150 ms for all three, a smaller bounce)?
While we're touching favourites: should the lock-screen / Control Center 'Like' command be wired up too? It is currently switched off (NowPlayingController.onLike is never set).
alternativeCauses: If skips still feel slower than play/pause after the 220 ms change, the likely cause is main-thread work in the same frame as the press. The skip action (AnimatedPlaybackControls.swift:80-82) synchronously triggers the song change: the carousel spring (AlbumCarousel.swift:109-113), the artwork and ambient background (PlayerAmbientBackground.swift:86-91), the Now Playing info and the re-theme. That can hitch the press spring's first frames. Measure on device first. Only if a hitch shows, try deferring the action, e.g. `Task { action() }`. A main-actor Task is not guaranteed to run after the next frame commits, so verify by recording. The older Android lineage deferred skips by 180 ms (main-6hltyd AnimatedPlaybackControls.kt:160-163); the newest Android branch (android-int-oct3 kt:173-176) calls them immediately, as iOS does.

Heart: ruled out an Equatable or memoised row (PlayerToggleRow has none), an async write (applyEdit is synchronous before the detached persistence write, LibraryEditing.swift:260-263), an identity reset (no `.id(...)` on the player), and a value captured at init (the value is recomputed every body pass; it just isn't tracked).
research:
Checked against Apple's documentation JSON (developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/…):

- ObservationIgnored: 'Disables observation tracking of a property … To prevent observation of an accessible property, attach the ObservationIgnored macro to the property' (iOS 17+, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/observation/observationignored()). This confirms that reads of `LibraryStore.songsById` never invalidate a view.
- View.layoutPriority(_:): 'Views typically have a default priority of 0 which causes space to be apportioned evenly to all sibling views … A parent layout offers the child views with the highest layout priority all the space offered to the parent minus the minimum space required for all its lower-priority children' (iOS 13+, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/layoutpriority(_:)). Priority therefore has to sit on the top bar's right-hand cluster, the Spacer's sibling, and not only on the pill. This corrects the previous plan.
- AVAudioSessionPortDescription.portName: 'A descriptive name for the port' (iOS 6+, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudiosessionportdescription/portname).
- Not documented by Apple, so treat it as empirical: the built-in speaker reports the portName 'Speaker'. That is why the phone case shows no label rather than the raw name.
- The previously cited forum thread (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/673999) could not be checked: the page is behind a bot check. Don't rely on it.

Android reference, /home/user/PixlAudio:
- main-6hltyd: AnimatedPlaybackControls.kt:96-105 (600 ms skip hold vs 220 ms releaseDelay) and :160-163/:242-245 (180 ms skip deferral); FullPlayerContent.kt:1182/1216-1217 (fastSpatialSpec, releaseDelay 220L); title hidden while casting at :724-725; cast pill at :781-880 (label only while casting or connecting, widthIn 50..190 or 50..58, dot only while remote).
- origin/android-int-oct3: the same 600L/220L and fastSpatialSpec (kt:103; FullPlayerContent.kt:1316/1375) and the same title hiding (:783), but no 180 ms skip deferral (kt:173-176).
